summary: Cambodia issues a 30-day tourist eVisa online (30 USD) and a 30 USD visa on arrival to most nationalities, while ASEAN neighbors enter visa-free. All travellers can submit the free Cambodia e-Arrival card within 7 days before arrival; Canada's travel advice says it must be completed.

declarations.name: Cambodia e-Arrival Card (CeA)
declarations.text: Cambodia's e-Arrival card combines the immigration, customs and health declarations in one online form (web or Cambodia e-Arrival app). The portal says all travellers can submit it within 7 days before their arrival and that submission is free; it lists Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville international airports. Canada's travel advice says the forms must be completed within 7 days of your scheduled arrival.

notes: Canada's travel advice says the Cambodia e-Arrival forms cover immigration, customs and health, and must be completed within 7 days of your scheduled arrival.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says US dollars are widely used alongside the riel, but only newer, undamaged notes are accepted — notes with the slightest tear are refused. Credit cards are not widely accepted outside major cities, and ATMs are plentiful in Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and Sihanoukville but fewer in smaller towns.

safety.text: The UK advises against all but essential travel within 20 km of the land border with Thailand, where landmines and unexploded ordnance also remain; Canada and Australia advise against all travel within 50 km of it, and the land crossings with Thailand are closed. Australia advises a high degree of caution in the rest of the country. The UK warns that most thefts are bag snatchings, often by thieves on motorbikes, and that organized crime groups run job scams advertising easy, well-paid work. Mined areas are often unmarked: the UK says not to stray off main routes in rural areas.

tips.text: The official eVisa site, run by Cambodia's foreign ministry, is evisa.gov.kh.
Bring US dollar notes in good condition: Canada's travel advice says only newer, undamaged notes are accepted, and Australia's Smartraveller says sellers may refuse dirty, torn or high-value notes.
The Cambodia e-Arrival card is free. All travellers can submit it within 7 days before arrival, at arrival.gov.kh or in the official Cambodia e-Arrival app.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Cambodia?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist visa: either the eVisa (30 USD, applied for at evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival (30 USD) at airports and major land borders; the land crossings with Thailand are currently closed. Both allow a 30-day stay; Canada's travel advice says a visa may be extended only once.

faq.question: Is the Cambodia eVisa better than the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: They cost the same (30 USD online or at the border) and both give 30 days. The eVisa is accepted only at the Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports and the Bavet and Trapeang Kriel land crossings — Cham Yeam and Poipet on the Thai border are temporarily closed to eVisa entry — so check your entry point first.

faq.question: What is the Cambodia e-Arrival card?
faq.answer: The Cambodia e-Arrival (CeA) is a free online form combining immigration, customs and health declarations, submitted within 7 days before arrival at arrival.gov.kh or via the Cambodia e-Arrival app. The portal says all travellers can submit it; Canada's travel advice says it must be completed within 7 days of your scheduled arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Cambodia?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says you can extend a tourist visa while in Cambodia. Canada's travel advice says visas must be renewed for stays over 30 days and may be extended only once. No official source we could read states the length of an extension or of the ordinary (E-class) visa's extensions.

faq.question: Which nationalities enter Cambodia visa-free?
faq.answer: The foreign ministry's list of visa exemptions gives ordinary passport holders of ASEAN countries visa-free entry: 30 days for Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Laos, Singapore and the Philippines, 14 days for Thailand, Myanmar and Brunei. Maldivian (30 days) and Seychellois (15 days) ordinary passports are also exempt.
